parts.stem: Some plant cells produce a polypeptide called systemin.
parts.text:
Describe the role of DNA in the production of systemin.

{{figure:reviewed_response_5.png}}

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.stem:
Systemin stimulates plant cells to produce enzyme inhibitors known as serpins.

One of these serpins is a competitive inhibitor of some protease enzymes. It inhibits the protease enzymes found in herbivores, but does **not** inhibit the proteases in plants.
parts.text:
Suggest how this serpin inhibits **only** the protease enzymes in herbivores but **not** those in plants.

{{figure:reviewed_response_6.png}}

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.stem: The presence of competitive inhibitors, such as serpins, increases the Michaelis-Menten constant ($K_m$) for the enzymes they inhibit.
